title: המחברת
subtitle: Hebrew from the first letter to B2: the alef-bet and nikud, then the grammar that makes the language click, with vocabulary, reading and flashcards built from it.

parts.title: Foundations
parts.blurb: Letters and vowels first, then enough grammar to build a sentence: the noun, the adjective, the present tense. Nothing here can be skipped, because everything after it assumes all of it.

chapters.title: The alef-bet
chapters.summary: The 22 letters, the sounds they carry, and the pairs that look alike on the page: ב כ, ד ר, ו ז, ח ה ת, ס ם.

chapters.title: Final letters, print and handwriting
chapters.summary: ך ם ן ף ץ, why five letters change shape at the end of a word, and what the same letters look like handwritten.

chapters.title: Nikud: the vowel points
chapters.summary: Kamatz, patach, segol, tzere, chirik, cholam, kubutz, shuruk, shva and the chataf vowels, and the five sounds they reduce to.

chapters.title: Dagesh, shin and sin
chapters.summary: בּ/ב, כּ/כ, פּ/פ, שׁ/שׂ: one dot that changes the sound, and one that changes the letter.

chapters.title: Vav and yod as vowels
chapters.summary: Full spelling: how ו and י stand in for cholam, shuruk and chirik once the points come off.

chapters.title: Stress and syllables
chapters.summary: Mil'ra and mil'el: Hebrew stresses the last syllable far more often than English expects, and the exceptions are learnable.

chapters.title: Reading without nikud
chapters.summary: What real Hebrew looks like: guessing the vowels from the root, the pattern, the context and the fifty words you already know.

chapters.title: Greetings and the first exchange
chapters.summary: שָׁלוֹם, מַה שְׁלוֹמְךָ, נָעִים מְאֹד, תּוֹדָה, בְּבַקָּשָׁה: enough to open and close a conversation before any grammar.

chapters.title: Nouns: gender and number
chapters.summary: The ה and ת that mark feminine, the ים and ות plurals, and the words that ignore both (שֻׁלְחָנוֹת, נָשִׁים).

chapters.title: The definite article ה
chapters.summary: One prefix for every noun, no gender and no number, and what happens when בְּ, לְ or כְּ is sitting in front of it.

chapters.title: Pronouns and the missing "is"
chapters.summary: אֲנִי, אַתָּה, אַתְּ, הוּא, הִיא and the rest, and why אֲנִי סְטוּדֶנְט is a complete sentence with no verb in it.

chapters.title: Adjectives
chapters.summary: After the noun, agreeing in gender, number and definiteness: הַבַּיִת הַגָּדוֹל, and the difference a ה makes.

chapters.title: This and that
chapters.summary: זֶה, זֹאת, אֵלֶּה standing alone, and הַזֶּה, הַזֹּאת attached to a definite noun.

chapters.title: Questions
chapters.summary: מַה, מִי, אֵיפֹה, מָתַי, לָמָּה, אֵיךְ, כַּמָּה, הַאִם, and the yes/no question that is only intonation.

chapters.title: Numbers 1 to 100
chapters.summary: Two sets of numbers, one per gender, why the feminine is the counting set, and אַחַת against אֶחָד.

chapters.title: Yesh and ein: there is, and having
chapters.summary: יֵשׁ and אֵין for existence, יֵשׁ לִי and אֵין לִי for possession, and why Hebrew has no verb "to have".

chapters.title: Prepositions with endings
chapters.summary: לְ, בְּ, שֶׁל, עִם, אֵצֶל, and the endings that turn each of them into לִי, לְךָ, לָךְ, שֶׁלִּי.

chapters.title: Et: the object marker
chapters.summary: The little word with no translation: when אֶת appears before an object, when it does not, and אוֹתִי, אוֹתְךָ.

chapters.title: Present tense: pa'al
chapters.summary: Four forms and no more: כּוֹתֵב, כּוֹתֶבֶת, כּוֹתְבִים, כּוֹתְבוֹת, on a root with three sound letters.

chapters.title: Present tense when a letter goes missing
chapters.summary: The verbs a beginner actually says: רוֹצֶה and קוֹנֶה, גָּר and קָם, קוֹרֵא and מוֹצֵא, and why each one is short a form.

chapters.title: Present tense: pi'el, hif'il, hitpa'el
chapters.summary: מְדַבֵּר, מַסְבִּיר, מִתְלַבֵּשׁ: recognising which binyan a verb is in from the shape of its present tense.

chapters.title: Negation
chapters.summary: לֹא before the verb, אֵין for existence, אַל for don't, and אַף אֶחָד for nobody.

chapters.title: Infinitives, wanting and having to
chapters.summary: לִכְתּוֹב, and the four words that take it: רוֹצֶה, צָרִיךְ, יָכוֹל, אוֹהֵב.

chapters.title: Time, days and where things are
chapters.summary: Days counted off the numbers, telling the time, בַּבֹּקֶר and בָּעֶרֶב, and כָּאן, שָׁם, פֹּה, עַכְשָׁיו, הַיּוֹם, מָחָר.

chapters.title: Smichut: two nouns as one
chapters.summary: בֵּית סֵפֶר, עוּגַת שׁוֹקוֹלָד: how Hebrew joins two nouns, and why the ה goes on the second one.

chapters.title: Was and will be
chapters.summary: הָיָה, הָיְתָה, הָיוּ, and יִהְיֶה: the verb that is missing in the present and obligatory everywhere else, including הָיָה לִי.

parts.title: Building fluency
parts.blurb: Past and future, and the system behind them. Three root letters and seven patterns turn out to generate most of the language, and this is where that stops being a claim and starts being useful.

chapters.title: Past tense: pa'al
chapters.summary: One stem, one suffix per person: כָּתַבְתִּי, כָּתַבְתָּ, כָּתַב, כָּתְבוּ, and the pronoun you can now leave out.

chapters.title: Past tense: the other binyanim
chapters.summary: דִּיבֵּר, הִסְבִּיר, הִתְלַבֵּשׁ, נִכְנַס: four different stems wearing the same set of endings.

chapters.title: Future tense
chapters.summary: A prefix for the person and a suffix for the number: the אֶ, תִּ, יִ, נִ row, in every binyan at once.

chapters.title: Weak roots
chapters.summary: ל"ה (לִרְאוֹת), פ"נ (לִנְסֹעַ), ע"ו (לָקוּם), פ"י (לָשֶׁבֶת) and the gutturals, across all three tenses.

chapters.title: Roots and patterns
chapters.summary: Three letters carry the meaning and a pattern carries the grammar: שֹׁרֶשׁ, בִּנְיָין and the mishkalim that build nouns.

chapters.title: The binyanim as a system
chapters.summary: Active, intensive, causative, reflexive, passive: what each of the seven does to the same three letters.

chapters.title: Commands and requests
chapters.summary: The written imperative, the future used as a command in speech, אַל for don't, and בְּבַקָּשָׁה doing the softening.

chapters.title: The relative ש
chapters.summary: One letter where English has who, which and that, plus the pronoun Hebrew leaves behind: הָאִישׁ שֶׁרָאִיתִי אוֹתוֹ.

chapters.title: Comparison and the most
chapters.summary: יוֹתֵר מִ, פָּחוֹת מִ, כְּמוֹ, and the הֲכִי that makes a superlative out of anything.

chapters.title: Adverbs and connectors
chapters.summary: מְאֹד, כְּבָר, עֲדַיִן, עוֹד, רַק, and the joins that turn sentences into paragraphs: אֲבָל, כִּי, לָכֵן, אָז.

chapters.title: Possession: shel and the endings
chapters.summary: הַסֵּפֶר שֶׁלִּי in speech, סִפְרִי in writing, and the family words that keep the old endings either way.

chapters.title: Prepositions that decline in the plural
chapters.summary: עָלַי, עָלֶיךָ, אֵלֶיהָ, לְפָנַי: the second declension, where the endings look plural and the meaning is not.

chapters.title: Direction and place
chapters.summary: הַבַּיְתָה and צָפוֹנָה, and the line between בְּ (in), לְ (to) and אֶל (towards).

chapters.title: If
chapters.summary: אִם for what may happen, and אִלּוּ or לוּ + הָיָה for what did not.

chapters.title: Ordinals, dates and the calendar
chapters.summary: רִאשׁוֹן, שֵׁנִי, שְׁלִישִׁי, how a date is written and said, and the Hebrew months you will meet on a holiday.

chapters.title: Numbers past a hundred, and the dual
chapters.summary: Hundreds, thousands, years and prices, plus the dual ending on יוֹמַיִם, שְׁבוּעַיִם, פַּעֲמַיִם.

chapters.title: Verbal nouns
chapters.summary: כְּתִיבָה, דִּבּוּר, הַסְבָּרָה, הִתְלַבְּשׁוּת: one noun shape per binyan, and how to read one you have never seen.

chapters.title: Reporting what someone said
chapters.summary: אָמַר שֶׁ, שָׁאַל אִם, and why Hebrew does not push the tense back the way English does.

chapters.title: Word order and emphasis
chapters.summary: Subject first by default, verb first for effect, and the אֶת that lets an object move to the front.

chapters.title: Reading a headline
chapters.summary: Newspaper Hebrew: no vowels, no verb, smichut chains stacked three deep, and the abbreviations everyone reads at a glance.

parts.title: Refining
parts.blurb: Longer sentences, the passive voice, and the difference between the Hebrew of a form and the Hebrew of a bus queue.

chapters.title: The passive binyanim
chapters.summary: פּוּעַל and הוּפְעַל: the two patterns with no infinitive, where they turn up, and why speech reaches for נִפְעַל instead.

chapters.title: Nif'al against hitpa'el
chapters.summary: Passive, reciprocal, reflexive and simply intransitive: the overlap between the two, and the line that still holds.

chapters.title: Cause and purpose
chapters.summary: בִּגְלַל and מִפְּנֵי שֶׁ for why it happened, כְּדֵי and לְמַעַן for what it was for, and לָכֵן for what followed.

chapters.title: Clauses of time and condition
chapters.summary: לִפְנֵי שֶׁ, אַחֲרֵי שֶׁ, כְּשֶׁ, בְּמִקְרֶה שֶׁ, and the tense that goes inside each of them.

chapters.title: Contrast and concession
chapters.summary: אֲבָל against אֶלָּא, לַמְרוֹת and אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁ, and בְּעוֹד שֶׁ for two things held side by side.

chapters.title: Making adjectives out of nouns
chapters.summary: The ending that turns אָבִיב into אֲבִיבִי and יִשְׂרָאֵל into יִשְׂרְאֵלִי, and how far it can be pushed.

chapters.title: Smichut in depth
chapters.summary: Construct plurals, chains of three, when שֶׁל is the better choice, and telling בֵּית סֵפֶר גָּדוֹל apart from בַּיִת גָּדוֹל.

chapters.title: Register: formal, spoken, slang
chapters.summary: One sentence at three heights, and where the spoken layer got its Arabic and Yiddish from.

chapters.title: Object endings on verbs
chapters.summary: רְאִיתִיו for רָאִיתִי אוֹתוֹ: reading the register that still writes it that way.

chapters.title: The spelling rules
chapters.summary: The Academy's rules for full spelling: where ו and י are written once the points are gone, and where they are not.

chapters.title: Biblical Hebrew in modern speech
chapters.summary: The vav that flips a tense, the archaic forms frozen inside idioms, and what is safe to skip.

chapters.title: Idioms and set phrases
chapters.summary: בְּעֶזְרַת הַשֵּׁם, עַל הַפָּנִים, סוֹף סוֹף, חֲבָל עַל הַזְּמַן, and forty more in the sentences they live in.

chapters.title: Pairs that catch everyone
chapters.summary: לָמָּה against מַדּוּעַ, אִם against עִם, בִּגְלַל against בִּשְׁבִיל, יָכוֹל against יוֹדֵעַ.

parts.title: Reference
parts.blurb: Tables to come back to rather than read through.

chapters.title: Alef-bet and nikud chart
chapters.summary: Every letter with its final form, name and sound, and every nikud sign with an example word, on one page.

chapters.title: Verb tables by binyan
chapters.summary: Present, past, future and infinitive for one sound root and one weak root in each of the seven binyanim.

chapters.title: Preposition tables
chapters.summary: The full declension of לְ, בְּ, שֶׁל, אֶת, עִם, עַל, אֶל, מִן and the rest, in one place.

chapters.title: How to use this course
chapters.summary: A route through the four parts, how much to take at a time, and what to do when a chapter will not stick.
